import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.5

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

If a finitely generated group is abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite, is it
isomorphic to a subgroup of the automorphism group of some finitely generated
metabelian group?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.5»

/-- For subgroups $A \le B$, the factor $B/A$ is cyclic if $A$ is normal in
$B$ and the corresponding quotient group is cyclic. -/
def IsCyclicFactor {G : Type*} [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ≤ B ∧ ∃ h : (A.subgroupOf B).Normal,
    letI := h
    IsCyclic (B ⧸ A.subgroupOf B)

/-- A group is polycyclic if it has a finite subnormal series whose factors
are cyclic. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s ⟨n, Nat.lt_succ_self n⟩ = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n, IsCyclicFactor (s i.castSucc) (s i.succ)

/-- A group is metabelian if its commutator subgroup is abelian. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/-- A group is abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite if it has an abelian normal
subgroup $A$ such that $G/A$ has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite
index. -/
def IsAbelianByPolycyclicByFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (A : Subgroup G) (hA : A.Normal), IsMulCommutative A ∧
    letI := hA
    ∃ (P : Subgroup (G ⧸ A)) (hP : P.Normal), IsPolycyclic P ∧
      letI := hP
      Finite ((G ⧸ A) ⧸ P)

/--
If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does
there exist a finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is
isomorphic to a subgroup of the automorphism group of $M$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (_ : Group.FG G),
      IsAbelianByPolycyclicByFinite G →
      ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Group M) (_ : Group.FG M),
        IsMetabelian M ∧ ∃ f : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.5»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite as the existence of an abelian normal subgroup A of G such that G/A has a normal polycyclic subgroup P of finite index.
Represented finite index of the normal subgroup P by finiteness of the quotient type (G/A)/P.
Defined polycyclicity by a finite ascending subnormal series from the trivial subgroup to the whole group, with every adjacent quotient cyclic.
Represented being isomorphic to a subgroup of the automorphism group by an injective group homomorphism G →* MulAut M.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.5

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there exist a
finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of the
automorphism group of $M$? If so, many of the tricky properties of $G$ like its residual
finiteness would become transparent.

Here a group is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ with all factors
$G_{i+1}/G_i$ cyclic, and it is *metabelian* if its commutator subgroup is abelian. For classes
of groups $\mathfrak{X}$ and $\mathfrak{Y}$, a group is $\mathfrak{X}$-by-$\mathfrak{Y}$ if it
has a normal subgroup in $\mathfrak{X}$ with quotient in $\mathfrak{Y}$. Thus $G$ is
abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite if it has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such that $G/A$ has a
polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.5»

/-- `IsPolycyclicOfLength n G` means that `G` has a subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$ of length $n$ in
which every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic. It is defined by recursion on $n$: a series of length
$0$ exists exactly when $G$ is trivial, and a series of length $n + 1$ exists exactly when $G$
has a normal subgroup $N$ with $G/N$ cyclic and $N$ having such a series of length $n$. -/
def IsPolycyclicOfLength : ℕ → (G : Type*) → [Group G] → Prop
  | 0, G, _ => Subsingleton G
  | n + 1, G, _ =>
    ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), IsPolycyclicOfLength n N ∧ IsCyclic (G ⧸ N)

/-- A group is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series with cyclic factors. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n, IsPolycyclicOfLength n G

/-- A group is *polycyclic-by-finite* if it has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index. -/
def IsPolycyclicByFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (P : Subgroup G) (_ : P.Normal), IsPolycyclic P ∧ P.FiniteIndex

/-- A group is *metabelian* if its commutator subgroup is abelian, i.e. it has derived length at
most $2$. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/-- The trivial group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨0, (inferInstance : Subsingleton G)⟩

/-- Every cyclic group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_isCyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨1, ⊥, inferInstance, (inferInstance : Subsingleton (⊥ : Subgroup G)),
    isCyclic_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).symm
      (QuotientGroup.quotientBot (G := G)).symm.surjective⟩

/-- Every finite group is polycyclic-by-finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclicByFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] :
    IsPolycyclicByFinite G :=
  ⟨⊥, inferInstance, isPolycyclic_of_subsingleton _, inferInstance⟩

/-- Every abelian group is metabelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsMulCommutative (commutator G))

/-- A group is metabelian if and only if its derived length is at most $2$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMetabelian G ↔ derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥ := by
  rw [IsMetabelian, derivedSeries_succ, derivedSeries_one,
    Subgroup.commutator_eq_bot_iff_le_centralizer, Subgroup.le_centralizer_iff_isMulCommutative]

/--
If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there exist a
finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of the
automorphism group of $M$?

Here $G$ is abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite if it has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such that
$G/A$ has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index. "$G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of
$\operatorname{Aut}(M)$" is stated as the existence of an injective group homomorphism
$G \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G],
      (∃ (A : Subgroup G) (_ : A.Normal),
        IsMulCommutative A ∧ IsPolycyclicByFinite (G ⧸ A)) →
      ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Group M), Group.FG M ∧ IsMetabelian M ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.5»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct: the problem is one yes/no question with an implicit universal quantifier over G, and the trailing sentence is motivation rather than a further question.
modeling_decisions: 'abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite' is read as abelian-by-(polycyclic-by-finite), as in the decomposition table: an abelian normal subgroup A with G/A having a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index. (The other bracketing, (abelian-by-polycyclic)-by-finite, defines the same class of groups: given N ⊴ G of finite index with abelian A ⊴ N and N/A polycyclic, the intersection of the finitely many G-conjugates of A is an abelian normal subgroup of G with the required quotient; the converse is immediate.)
'G is isomorphic to a subgroup of Aut(M)' is formalized as `∃ φ : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective φ`; `MulAut M` is Mathlib's group of multiplicative (i.e. group) automorphisms of M.

Both G and M are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the repository's Kourovka idiom. This loses no generality: finitely generated groups are countable, hence isomorphic to groups in `Type`.
'Finitely generated' is `Group.FG`. 'Finite index' is `Subgroup.FiniteIndex` (index ≠ 0). 'Abelian normal subgroup' is `A.Normal` with `IsMulCommutative A`.
`IsCyclic` in Mathlib includes the trivial group and infinite cyclic groups, matching the usual definition of polycyclic (factors may be finite or infinite cyclic, possibly trivial).

The hypotheses of the ∀ are placed after the quantified G as an implication (`(∃ A …) → ∃ M …`), avoiding the `∃ x, P x → Q` pitfall; the hypothesis is satisfiable (e.g. G = ℤ), so the statement is not vacuous.
The final sentence of the problem ('If so, many of the tricky properties…') is motivation and appears only in the module docstring, not in the formal statement.

subgroup of the automorphism group of $M$?

namespace Kourovka.«5.5»

/-- `HasCyclicSeries n G` says that the group `G` has a subnormal series of length `n`
with cyclic factors, i.e. $G = G_n \trianglerighteq G_{n-1} \trianglerighteq \dots
\trianglerighteq G_0 = 1$ with every $G_{i+1} / G_i$ cyclic. It is defined by recursion:
a series of length `0` means `G` is trivial, and a series of length `n + 1` consists of a
normal subgroup `N` of `G` with `G ⧸ N` cyclic together with a series of length `n` for `N`. -/
def HasCyclicSeries : ℕ → (G : Type*) → [Group G] → Prop
  | 0, G, _ => Subsingleton G
  | n + 1, G, _ => ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), IsCyclic (G ⧸ N) ∧ HasCyclicSeries n N

/-- A group is polycyclic if it has a subnormal series with cyclic factors. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, HasCyclicSeries n G

/-- A group is polycyclic-by-finite if it has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index. -/
def IsPolycyclicByFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Subgroup G, P.Normal ∧ IsPolycyclic P ∧ P.FiniteIndex

/-- A group is abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite if it has an abelian normal subgroup `A`
such that `G ⧸ A` is polycyclic-by-finite. -/
def IsAbelianByPolycyclicByFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (A : Subgroup G) (_ : A.Normal), IsMulCommutative A ∧ IsPolycyclicByFinite (G ⧸ A)

/-- A group is metabelian if its commutator subgroup is abelian. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/-- The trivial group is polycyclic. -/

theorem isPolycyclic_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨0, ‹_›⟩

/-- Cyclic groups are polycyclic. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_isCyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨1, ⊥, inferInstance, isCyclic_of_surjective _ (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective ⊥),
    (inferInstance : Subsingleton (⊥ : Subgroup G))⟩

/-- Abelian groups are metabelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G :=
  ⟨⟨fun a b => Subtype.ext (mul_comm (a : G) b)⟩⟩

If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there
exist a finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a
subgroup of the automorphism group of $M$?

"$G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$" is stated as the existence
of an injective group homomorphism $G \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$.

    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G], IsAbelianByPolycyclicByFinite G →
      ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Group M), Group.FG M ∧ IsMetabelian M ∧
        ∃ f : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.5»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.5

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there
exist a finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a
subgroup of the automorphism group of $M$?

Wehrfritz remarks that a positive answer would make many of the tricky
properties of $G$, like its residual finiteness, transparent.

Here "$\mathfrak{X}$-by-$\mathfrak{Y}$" means having a normal subgroup in
$\mathfrak{X}$ with quotient in $\mathfrak{Y}$. A group is *polycyclic* if it has
a subnormal series with cyclic factors, and *metabelian* if its commutator
subgroup is abelian.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.5»

/-- A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$
all of whose factors $H_{i+1} / H_i$ are cyclic. -/
def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, ∃ (_ : H i.castSucc ≤ H i.succ)
      (_ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal),
      IsCyclic (H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ))

/-- A group $G$ is *metabelian* if its commutator subgroup $[G, G]$ is abelian,
i.e. if $G$ has derived length at most $2$. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/-- The trivial group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_subsingleton (G : Type*) [Group G] [Subsingleton G] :
    IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨0, fun _ => ⊥, rfl, Subsingleton.elim _ _, fun i => i.elim0⟩

/-- Every cyclic group is polycyclic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isPolycyclic_of_isCyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] [IsCyclic G] : IsPolycyclic G :=
  ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
    refine ⟨bot_le, inferInstance, ?_⟩
    have : IsCyclic (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
      isCyclic_of_surjective Subgroup.topEquiv.symm Subgroup.topEquiv.symm.surjective
    exact isCyclic_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.mk' _) (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)⟩

/-- Every abelian group is metabelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G := by
  unfold IsMetabelian
  infer_instance

/--
If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, i.e. $G$ is finitely
generated and has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such that $G / A$ has a polycyclic normal
subgroup of finite index, does there exist a finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that
$G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup of the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(M)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G] (A : Subgroup G) [A.Normal], IsMulCommutative A →
      (∃ P : Subgroup (G ⧸ A), P.Normal ∧ P.FiniteIndex ∧ IsPolycyclic P) →
      ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Group M), Group.FG M ∧ IsMetabelian M ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.5»

$1 = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$

  ∃ P : Subgroup G, P.Normal ∧ P.FiniteIndex ∧ IsPolycyclic P

/-- A group is *metabelian* if its commutator subgroup is abelian. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

  refine ⟨1, ![⊥, ⊤], rfl, rfl, fun i => ?_⟩

    isCyclic_of_surjective (QuotientGroup.mk' _) (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _)⟩

theorem IsMetabelian.of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G :=
  Subgroup.commGroup_isMulCommutative _

/--
If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there
exist a finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to
a subgroup of the automorphism group of $M$?

Here the first condition means that $G$ has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such
that $G/A$ has a normal polycyclic subgroup of finite index. Metabelian means
that the second term of the derived series is trivial.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Group.FG G],
      (∃ A : Subgroup G, ∃ hA : A.Normal,
        IsMulCommutative A ∧
          let _ := hA
          ∃ P : Subgroup (G ⧸ A), P.Normal ∧ IsPolycyclic P ∧ P.FiniteIndex) →
      ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Group M) (_ : Group.FG M),
        derivedSeries M 2 = ⊥ ∧
          ∃ f : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective f := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 5.5

by B. A. F. Wehrfritz

If $G$ is a finitely generated abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite group, does there
exist a finitely generated metabelian group $M$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a
subgroup of the automorphism group of $M$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«5.5»

universe u

/-- A group is polycyclic if it can be built in finitely many steps from cyclic
factors. Equivalently, it has a finite subnormal series with cyclic factors. -/
inductive IsPolycyclic : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop
  | cyclic (G : Type u) [Group G] (_ : IsCyclic G) : IsPolycyclic G
  | extension (G : Type u) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal]
      (_ : IsCyclic (G ⧸ N)) (_ : IsPolycyclic N) : IsPolycyclic G

/-- A group is metabelian if its commutator subgroup is abelian. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/--
If $G$ is finitely generated and has an abelian normal subgroup $A$ such that
$G/A$ has a polycyclic normal subgroup of finite index, does there exist a
finitely generated metabelian group $M$ and an injective group homomorphism
$G \to \operatorname{Aut}(M)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«5.5» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (_ : Group.FG G),
      (∃ (A : Subgroup G) (_ : A.Normal), IsMulCommutative A ∧
        ∃ (P : Subgroup (G ⧸ A)) (_ : P.Normal), IsPolycyclic P ∧ P.FiniteIndex) →
      ∃ (M : Type) (_ : Group M) (_ : Group.FG M), IsMetabelian M ∧
        ∃ φ : G →* MulAut M, Function.Injective φ := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«5.5»
modeling_decisions: Expanded “abelian-by-polycyclic-by-finite” as the existence of an abelian normal subgroup A of G such that G/A contains a normal polycyclic subgroup P of finite index, following the fixed decomposition.

Modeled polycyclic groups inductively: cyclic groups are polycyclic, and a group with a polycyclic normal subgroup and cyclic quotient is polycyclic. This is equivalent to having a finite subnormal series with cyclic factors.
Modeled metabelianity by requiring Mathlib's commutator subgroup to be abelian, which gives derived length at most two.
Modeled “isomorphic to a subgroup of the automorphism group” as an injective group homomorphism G →* MulAut M.
